title: Cloud-Native & Legacy Modernization

meta_description: Cloud-Native & Legacy Modernization from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: How Dataq Software delivers Cloud-Native & Legacy Modernization — bounded scope, a fixed weekly cadence, the platforms it runs on, and outcomes written into the contract.

Legacy modernization fails when it is a rewrite project; it succeeds when it is a strangler-pattern program with business metrics. We decompose monoliths along domain seams (event-storming first), route traffic incrementally, and retire components on a schedule the business can see — each wave priced in reduced maintenance cost, deployment lead time and incident load, not just in technology fashion.

The modernization stack is standard and boring on purpose: containers on Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD with progressive delivery, observability from day one. For mainframe estates we add automated code analysis, data-state replay testing, and parallel-run verification — because regulated workloads must prove equivalence before cutover, not after an apology.

The rhythm is fixed on purpose: progress becomes visible from week one, not after the first steering meeting. The first two weeks lock the baseline: your team and ours measure the current metric together and sign it. Weeks 3–8 carry the pilot on bounded scope — a single decision path, workflow, plant or portfolio — and a control owner on your side owns the evidence. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement, and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Missing a gate produces a documented decision to stop or redirect — never a silent extension.
